title: Delight in Union
note: Having read her signs and come together with her, the man speaks of his delight in that union.

couplets.plain: All that the five senses know, by seeing, hearing, tasting, smelling and touching, is here in her of the bright bangles.
couplets.pm: What the eye sees, the ear hears, the tongue tastes, the nose smells and the skin touches are all found in this woman of the bright bangles, and nowhere else. What is enjoyed at different times through different things is enjoyed at one time in her. The acts of lovemaking set out in Sanskrit works are included too.
couplets.context: He says this at the end of their first union.
couplets.speaker: he

links.quote: All that the five senses know

couplets.plain: The medicine for an illness is something else. For the sickness this jewelled woman gives, she herself is the medicine.
couplets.pm: Medicines for illnesses such as disorders of wind are opposite in nature to the cause. Not so with this jewelled woman: for the sickness that comes from her, she herself is the medicine. He had been suffering at the memory of their first union, and his pain ended when he met her alone at that place. No easy remedy could have cured him.
couplets.context: He says this when he meets her again at the same place.
couplets.speaker: he

links.reason: Gives desire’s odd rule: the one who causes the sickness is the one who cures it.

links.quote: The medicine for an illness is something else
links.reason: Sets this sickness against every other illness, whose cure lies somewhere other than its cause.

couplets.plain: Is the world of the lotus-eyed one sweeter than sleep on the soft shoulders of the one you love?
couplets.pm: Can the world of Vishnu, which ascetics reach by renouncing the five senses, be reached as painlessly as sleep on the soft shoulders of the woman you desire? It means giving up such sleep and suffering in austerities, so it isn’t for people like us. He rejects the reading that this is Indra’s world, because lotus-eyed is no name of Indra.
couplets.context: His companion tells him that someone fit for the highest joy shouldn’t be brought so low by this small pleasure. He answers.
couplets.speaker: he

links.quote: sleep on the soft shoulders of the one you love
links.reason: Asks whether the world of the lotus-eyed one could be sweeter than sleep on soft shoulders.

couplets.plain: It burns when you move away and cools when you come near. Where did she get this fire?
couplets.pm: This fire burns when you leave it and cools when you come close. In what world did she get it, to give to me? Before union he suffers and after it he is happy, and no such fire exists on earth. The fire of desire is his own, but he says she gave it, because she is what brings it out.
couplets.context: He says this after a meeting his companion has arranged.
couplets.speaker: he

links.quote: It burns when you move away and cools when you come near
links.reason: He pictures a fire of hers that burns from far off and cools when close.

couplets.plain: The shoulders of this woman with flowers in her hair are like whatever you want, just when you want it.
couplets.pm: However often you have them, the shoulders of this woman with flowers in her thick hair give joy, as each sweet thing does when it comes just as you are longing for it. They have already met three times, yet her shoulders bind his heart as if new. He has never had enough.
couplets.context: He says this after a meeting her friend has arranged.
couplets.speaker: he

links.quote: like whatever you want, just when you want it

couplets.plain: Each time I touch her, my life puts out new leaves. This innocent girl’s shoulders must be made of ambrosia.
couplets.pm: My life withered without her, and each time I reach her, her touch makes it put out new leaves. So this innocent girl’s shoulders are made of an ambrosia you can touch. He says this because they revive a withered life. New leaves here means flourishing with joy.
couplets.context: He goes on, after the meeting her friend has arranged.
couplets.speaker: he

links.reason: Her shoulders are made of the food of immortality, since touching them makes his life put out new leaves.

links.quote: my life puts out new leaves
links.reason: Each touch of hers makes his life put out new leaves.

couplets.plain: Embracing this woman of lovely complexion is like staying in your own home and eating your share of what is yours.
couplets.pm: In the joy it gives, her embrace is like staying in your own home and eating your share of what your own labour earned, after giving out to the ancestors, the gods, guests and kin. He is refusing marriage: this union already gives me the heaven that householders reach.
couplets.context: Her friend tells him to marry her and take up household life, where people live at home and share what they have. He answers.
couplets.speaker: he

links.quote: like staying in your own home and eating your share of what is yours

couplets.plain: For two who love each other, it is sweet: an embrace that not even the air can cut through.
couplets.pm: An embrace that never loosens for a moment, so that the wind can’t cut through it, is surely sweet to two who long for each other. But there are no two here, so this doesn’t apply to us. He delights in their secret union and won’t agree to marriage.
couplets.note: The words praise the close embrace. He says the man is refusing marriage: such an embrace suits two people, and these two are already one.
couplets.context: Her friend urges marriage, saying that for two so matched in loving-kindness an embrace that never ends is sweetest. He answers.
couplets.speaker: he

links.quote: an embrace that not even the air can cut through

couplets.plain: Sulking, making up and coming together: these are what those who have joined in desire get from it.
couplets.pm: Sulking, ending it in due measure, and the union that follows: this is what married people get. The man goes away to courtesans, she learns of it and sulks, the guilty man protests his innocence, and they join again. We share one life, like the two-headed bird, and we need none of it. He is scorning marriage.
couplets.note: The words praise sulking, making up and union. He hears scorn: the man lists what married people get and says the two of them need none of it.
couplets.context: Her friend urges marriage: a union with no hiding and no break is the one that brings joy. He answers.
couplets.speaker: he

links.quote: Sulking, making up and coming together

links.reason: Making up and coming together are named as what desire pays out.

links.quote: those who have joined in desire

couplets.plain: Each thing you learn shows up your ignorance. Desire is like that, each time I hold this woman in red jewels close.
couplets.pm: As you learn through books and fine perception, what you knew before shows up as ignorance. So with my desire for her, each time I hold her. Secrecy kept him from her, and now he has her always. Knowledge has no limit and nor has closeness, so each embrace seems not close enough. She delights in union too, but only by signs, never in words.
couplets.context: He has joined her and is going away with her, and says this to himself.
couplets.speaker: he

links.quote: Desire is like that, each time I hold this woman in red jewels close
links.reason: Desire grows with each embrace, as learning only uncovers more ignorance.

ideaLinks.quote: Desire is like that, each time I hold this woman in red jewels close
ideaLinks.reason: Each time he holds her close his desire grows, as learning only deepens the sense of ignorance.
